correctness.rationale: For even b≥2 and positive d|b−1, n=d(b+1), N divisible by n forces d|s_b(N) from b≡1 mod d and E−O≡0 mod(b+1) from b≡−1 mod(b+1). Since an odd u≤b−1 has nonzero odd E−O of absolute size <b+1, it is impossible. For sufficiency, A=∑_{j=0}^{2d−1}b^j has digit sum 2d and is divisible by d(b+1); B=b⁴+db²+(d−1)b+(b−1) has sum b−1+2d and is likewise divisible by coprime factors d,b+1. Concatenating the representations gives all even multiples of d and all odd multiples above b−1. There are ((b−1)/d+1)/2 gaps, largest b−1, density 1/d. Independent finite-state arbitrary-length search compared 364 target sums for tested small even bases/divisors; unbounded parameters follow only from proof.
residual_risks: Even-base restriction essential to odd parity of d and b−1.
The result counts attainable digit-sum values, not multiplicities or least positive multipliers.
